steps.content: Once the sandstorm calms down a little, you prepare to go to Bryce's ship with a few crew members and Eirene.
From afar, the gold watch on the wrist of that wrinkled hand drooping from the artillery is still glistening even in this gloomy weather.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: It's indeed... him.
...You didn't have to come.
Eirene shakes her head and says thanks to you, then turns around to walk toward the cockpit.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I'm just here to take one last look at him... I'll wait for you in the cockpit, Chief.
You watch Eirene enter the cabin, take a deep breath, then begin handling the dead body lying over the artillery.
Although your bullets missed, the navigator's didn't. The filth oozing out from the wound is pooling around the other cheek, dying the still-open eyes a different color.
This is...?
You put on a pair of gloves and gently pull the body's eyes open, examining them carefully.
His eyes have been tampered with?

The liquid is flowing into the eyes in a weird direction, as if it's seeping in. When you look more closely, you find that the two eyes are looking to the left and right in a strange way, as if they haven't been properly installed.
A layer of cold sweat breaks all over your back: this isn't Bryce!!
You force yourself to calm down and mentally go through all the events in order...
Eirene... you've led me here.
From the very beginning, the person who lured you to this area to fight the freighters and told you that your assailant was Bryce... has been Eirene!
Now that you're sailing on an unrecorded route because you've been attacked, without Eirene's help, you certainly won't be able to make it out of here.
You leave two people here to take care of Bryce and walk out of the cockpit gloomily.
Chief? You're already done... taking care of him?
A clear voice sounds in a dark corner. A grim white light is turned out with a click, illuminating both you and her.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Why the long face? You can't be mourning for that man... can you?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Don't worry, he's long gotten his hands dirty... with many things, including the blood of his own kin.
Since the start of the chess match, you've been planning all of this, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Haha... Chief, I recall I already told you this when we first had a heart-to-heart.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Businesspeople... always seek to maximize their profits.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: In chess, there's an opening known as the Queen's Gambit. It's a very risky move, so few are willing to use it. Those who do are mostly highly skilled... or simply arrogant.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Obviously... I am both.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I made myself a pawn and rushed to you during the opening... I was glad you didn't block me in the middle, you let me come to the end smoothly... Now, I've turned the pawn back into the queen.
You do have masterful chess skills, but this is not what I want to hear.
State your request plainly.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I like talking business with smart people.

Eirene leans back and sits in the leather chair in the cockpit. Ignoring the faint smell of gunpowder and blood, you find that she does look like the kind of CEO ready to sign a contract you've seen on TV.

options: Is this another plan instructed by Bryce?

choices.text: Is this another plan instructed by Bryce?

steps.content: This is... indeed ruthless.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Haha... First of all, I believe you understand the current situation. That's why you came to me alone.
Yes, I must admit I need your help to get out of here.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But the truth is that you can also threaten me with the shackles and make me escort you out without harming you.
I want the truth more than that.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You can also use the shackles to...
I've said it before, Eirene. I've always firmly believed that the shackles do not exist to suppress your freedom.
Eirene rests her elbows on the armrests and crosses her two hands, staring at you intensely.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Alright. Since you have a clear understanding of your situation and are so merciful, Chief, I'll be upfront with you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: My request is simple: be my cover in Syndicate.
Be your cover in Syndicate...? You do want to get involved in the private mines, after all!
It seems like you've already begun your moves in Syndicate... Bishop is indeed working with you, am I right?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Yes, this lucrative business has been getting divided by Syndicans little by little for a long time. How can the Campbells just sit back and watch? That's the Hypercube we're talking about!
Eirene lifts a hand, as if giving a business talk.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But as you know, those gangsters, those Sinners loitering in Syndicate... are no pushovers.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Besides... I need the name of an official entity. I don't want to taint Quinn's reputation.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: The chief of the MBCC, my friend... you're the most suitable person.
I don't seem to have the right to say no.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Haha, of course you do, Chief.
Eirene covers her mouth and chuckles, then lifts her hand again. In the silence, you hear the clicks of numerous guns being loaded.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But if you choose to say no, you leave me with no choice but to hold a grand farewell party for you and me.
You and me?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: The poor chief of the MBCC died in a desert bandit attack when he took his Sinner to WhiteSands. They both died under gunfire.
steps.female_content: The poor chief of the MBCC died in a desert bandit attack when she took her Sinner to WhiteSands. They both died under gunfire.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But only you will really die, as for me... I will be reborn in Syndicate. My past will be erased, I'll build another empire with a new identity.
Syndicans, especially those gangsters, won't trust a newcomer blindly.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: As long as they can't tell I'm a newcomer, it'll be fine. That can be achieved easily, Chief.
...Enoch. He'll forge a new identity for you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You're indeed very smart, Chief. Sadly, you're always one step behind me.
You take a deep breath, and breathe out while shaking your head. You give her a faint smile the way she does.
When I was reading the rules of chess, I learned about a move... called castling.
Although I indeed lost to you in that game... I may not lose this one.
You walk to the chair facing Eirene and sit down, staring at her eyes of different colors.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Oh? Your growth is so rapid... A pleasant surprise.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You do implement your strategy very... decisively, Chief. Now I'm glad you're not in business.
When we first found that batch of goods, we had our reservations. In fact, I checked the shipping manifests between Fraser City and the DisCity in the past eight years.
Indeed, I couldn't retrieve the records from several years, but just from the available data from the first few years, I could observe some irregularities.
Eirene frowns slightly and signals you to continue with her gaze. It feels like the two of you are back to the interrogation room.
Like with most Outland cities, the trade between Fraser City and the DisCity mostly involves exchanging household goods and energy with precious metals.

But starting eight years ago, the household goods and energy exported to Outland have been decreasing each year. Lately, it's been found that the imported precious metals have been gradually replaced by DisCoins of the equivalent weight...

As far as I know, during this period, Fraser City didn't suffer any large-scale diseases, natural disasters, or arable land degradation caused by industrial factors, so there hasn't been a decline in its population.
Then... what caused the reduction in the exported energy and household goods? Where... did this amount of DisCity cash come from?
Eirene still wears the same poised expression, but her palms are pressed together. Like white sand, the pale color resulting from the pressure on the muscles and joints has covered her fingers.
My guess is that... Fraser City has probably switched owners through some unspeakable means. And its new owner is Quinn's CEO who holds the massive cash flow in her hands, Miss Eirene.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Your thoughts are... very cruel.
Yes, it makes me instinctively want to believe your story.
But luckily... even in the face of a master, my chess skills are not exactly horrible.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: ...Haha... Hahahaha!
This is the first time you've seen Eirene lose her cool. Though half of her pretty face is masked by her hand, when the laughter stops, those eyes are sending you an obvious warning.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You're right, Chief. Fraser City has indeed switched owners in a ruthless way.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: When I awakened as a Sinner, Bryce initially wanted to control me and use me for his great comeback plan.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But just as you've said, how can an ordinary man subdue a Sinner? Besides... isn't Bryce exactly the type who doesn't give a damn about his own family?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Perhaps I should put it this way... Our relationship completely fell apart in that explosion in WhiteSands.
Eirene's voice is dull. She raises her head and looks around the cabin to find that logo projected above the control panel. The Campbell family's coat of arms.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Or perhaps even earlier? When my mother passed away having never earned a legitimate place beside him, all he did was come to play chess with me. It was the only game I've ever won against him.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But I don't want to become the next Bryce.

The image on the projected screen suddenly changes from the coat of arms to somewhere like a monitoring room. On the screen, a blond old man is sitting in a wheelchair and staring at the empty chessboard before him blankly.
Is that Bryce?!

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: That's right. I couldn't bring myself to kill my dear father just like that... He still has to witness how I'll become the Campbells' pride.
What have you done to him...?!

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: He's old and he treasures his life... He almost never questions whether the pills he takes every day are really going to make him live longer.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But what does that matter, Chief?
Eirene's tone has regained its usual coolness, questioning you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You don't think you'll be able to beat me just because you have this information, do you?
Of course I can't. I know that.
But it puts me in a state where I can assess the trade between us more... fairly.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: What state?
You straighten up and lean forward, shortening the distance between you and Eirene.
Based on the assumption I've mentioned, when I invited you to Fraser City... I also requested armed protection from the 9th Agency.
Before we boarded the ship, a team of armed guards has been placed in different parts of the sand cruiser.
Otherwise, why would I dare to come to meet you alone?
You see Eirene frown. Obviously, she didn't expect you'd hidden help on the sand cruiser.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Ha... I thought you said the main purpose this time wasn't a violent confrontation?
I meant not with Bryce Campbell.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But this is pointless, Chief. Without me, you guys can't make it out of this desert.

While you pretended to be dodging the freighters' attacks, you damaged the sand cruiser's communication and positioning functions. But you probably didn't expect that every member sent by the 9th Agency has their own positioning device on them.
All I need to do is survive until they make it here, that's it. Please do not underestimate the 9th Agency.
Eirene lowers her hand, the smile on her face deepening. She's watching you like you're a precious gem.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I really admire you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I did... underestimate you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But unfortunately...
Eirene stands up and comes behind you. She places her hands on the armrests of your chair, almost encircling you with her body.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I, Eirene Campbell, belong to the Campbell family. I've been the Campbell family's head for the past eight years.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I've watched sand cruisers come and go, float and sink, since I was a child.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: The weight of goods and the number of people a sand cruiser is carrying... I can tell these just from the speed it's going at, the draft, and the area of the sand it's stirring up.
Eirene's voice rings by your ear, as if whispering to you. Her warm breaths are spraying on your ear, but you're feeling an icy chill on your back.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Still, I do really appreciate you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Since the moment you accepted my invitation despite not knowing all the rules of chess...

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Perhaps... you'll make a pretty good opponent.
What do you want?
Eirene sits back into the chair facing you, reaching out a hand to you with amusement.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You already know my plan, and I understand your ideas.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Right now, it's safe to say... we're at even strength.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: In that case... I'd like to have another game of chess with you.
What kind of chess?
Several rays of sunlight shine through the gap shattered by the shells, cutting up the shadows between you and Eirene and forming a chessboard on the coffee table.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I'll return to the MBCC with you and accept your detention arrangements. I know that according to the rules, they won't ask me to give up Quinn just like that, so I'll still have the time and rights for my personal activities.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: What do you think? Will you accept my challenge? The chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control who refuses to control me with the shackles... The chief who's competent enough to be my opponent.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Well... I look forward to finding out who'll come out the winner in this even match.
If we're no longer bound by the rules of chess, then I guess, there can be more outcomes than just victory or loss.
You grip Eirene's extended hand. Her warm palm grips yours and pulls you forward...

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Very well... Let's find out together.
